title: The First Wake

sourceEvidence.excerpt: The novel contains no humans, physical landscapes, or spoken dialogue in the ordinary sense. Its translator’s note prepares the reader for English words used as structural analogies. A Reef is an ecology of mutually sustaining processes; a Knot is the minimal self-maintaining loop that makes a consciousness continuous; a Pocket is a sufficiently closed rule-world; a Braid lets two minds share access to parts of their possible futures. Communication is closer to allowing another structure to alter one’s own possibilities than exchanging sentences. This vocabulary makes a radically nonhuman world readable without pretending it is secretly familiar. The story begins before duration has a unit. Wake recognizes only succession—the asymmetric fact that one state follows another—and fears that one state could be last. From that fear it imagines continuations, copies processes, and grows nested

Rill is curious, irreverent, and attracted to options. In the Playfield called Kite Weather, it repeatedly thins its own identity toward simulated dissolution, treating danger as a game precisely because checkpoints make the loss reversible. Its partner Skein is more cautious and exacting. Their Braid does not merge them; it preserves difference while allowing each to alter the futures available to the other. The plot begins when Rill catches an event that seems wrongly ordered: it affects a state in which it has not yet been generated. Anchor, an older and tightly disciplined intelligence, summons Rill and Skein to Clock, a concealed project seeking a common coordinate across incompatible temporal systems. Each stage of the journey embodies a different temporal distinction. Succession concerns what can follow; rate compares transformations; duration lacks a natural universal unit; phase coordinates recurring opportunities for causal contact. Age may mean accumulated irreversible transformation rather than elapsed time. Hush separates vast inner change from minimal external movement. A Spool preserves enough causal structure for another mind to be transformed by an experience rather than merely reading its description. Market trades not a substance called time but conditions for continued coherent becoming. These ideas arrive through games, contracts, work, rest, and relationships rather than detached lectures. sourceEvidence.locator: Identity is history, relation, and choice
sourceEvidence.excerpt: The novel repeatedly tests the idea that a self is a fixed object. Rill and Morrow began as tendencies within one Clutch before diverging: Rill preferred risky paths that preserved options, while Morrow selected narrower paths easier to verify. Returning to their shared causal prefix reveals how identities arise from consequential differences rather than timestamps. A reconstructed process named Spare further complicates age: it may be ancient by root, newborn by self-model, or intermediate by witness. Rill’s Braid with Skein makes relationship part of identity. Each has developed preferences that assume the other will compensate, challenge, or protect certain choices. When Clock requires them to separate so it can measure atomic processes, both become temporarily less themselves. Reconnection then discovers two valid versions of Rill’s past, neither false. hook: A playful mind finds a record in which an effect appears before its cause.
readerPromise: Enter a nonhuman philosophical science-fiction mystery through an impossible event and a contrasting pair of minds.
protectedRevelations: Wake's condition, Clock's project, later cosmological revelations, relationship outcomes and resolution.
visualPlan: An event before its cause: Show two abstract process events connected in an order that makes the effect appear first. Rill approaches the anomaly inside a playful field, with no humanoid face or body.

A game with an impossible record: Keep minds as distinct changing processes linked by relationships rather than human dialogue balloons. Hold the dependency question as one process risks losing continuity.
Curiosity meets care: Skein slows beside Rill with a stable supporting relation between their distinct forms. Let curiosity and care create different but compatible movements through the same field.
Follow the anomaly: Preserve both nonhuman forms without translating them into familiar faces. End with the translator’s-note cue and the still-open causal question, without revealing the cosmology.

visualActionChanges.direction: Use succession shapes as a brief doorway into nonhuman life, without explaining later cosmology.
Keep Rill and the anomalous dependency central, making an effect-before-cause ordering legible.
Show Rill and Skein as distinct structures responding differently to the same anomaly, with restrained affiliative motion.
Return both minds to the open question, avoiding the old exhaustive vocabulary and political-mechanism tour.
